text.p: Summit Technology Inc said on Friday that chief executive officer and chairman David Muller's employment has been terminated by the board of directors.
Summit added that the board has appointed an executive committee which will be chaired by presdient Verne Sharma, who will also serve as interim CEO.

Richard Miller, a board member speaking on behalf of the board said in a statement "It is now time for the company to focus on the bottom line. We believe that Mr. Sharma and his team have the ability to accomplish our goals."
The executive committee has been charged to "identify and evaluate strategic options designed to achieve profitability" and position Summit for future growth, it said.

"We intend to concentrate on revenue enhancement, cost containment and improving customer relations. I am confident that we can create a successful company and realize our goal of commercializing laser vision correction technology and bringing its benefits to millions of people worldwide."

Last month, a class action lawsuit was filed against Summit on behalf of shareholders who purchased its stock between May 12 1995 and July 3 1996, alleging illegal sales of a laser which treats nearsightedness.
The suit also charged that Muller had received confidential and proprietary information about a similar laser made by its competitor VISX Inc in November 1995.
The suit charges that based on this non-public information, Muller and other top officers unloaded millions of dollars worth of Summit stock.
Muller and Summit company officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
